page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.sn2.xlarge delivers modest performance relative to modern hardware classes. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read-only performance, though large-block write operations achieve average tier results. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression, perform poorly, ranking in the bottom 10% of tested servers. However, the processor supports AVX and AVX-512F instruction sets, which helps maintain average performance in Passmark CPU extended instruction tests and small-scale LLM inference tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2.xlarge offers a dedicated resource allocation without the premium cost of high-frequency compute or memory-optimized instances. The lack of bundled local storage and modest network throughput of 2 Gbps represent clear tradeoffs for data-intensive applications. This server is best aligned with general-purpose workloads that require dedicated CPU cores but do not demand high-throughput I/O or extreme computational speed, such as basic web serving, small database operations, and lightweight application hosting.
